quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All of it

questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-fourths of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help reduce your chances of a crash?

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Show your intentions by using turn signals and brake light.
Look for hazards in your path.
Hope that other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope that other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, communicate your intentions, and stay aware of hazards. Do not depend on hoping other drivers see you. Instead, actively work to be seen and prepared for emergencies.

questions.question: What should a rain suit do?

options.text: Not be used at all.
Not puff up when you ride.
Not be needed since you should not ride in rain.
Tear easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not puff up when you ride.
questions.explanation: A good rain suit for motorcycles will not tear and will not puff up when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Keep riding and let it correct itself.
Brake hard and fast.
Reduce speed by closing the throttle slowly.
Speed up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed by closing the throttle slowly.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down gradually, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Then check what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: How fast should you ride at night?

options.text: Slower than you would during the day.
At the same speed as during the day.
Faster than you would during the day.
On the road shoulder so others can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than during the day under the same weather and traffic conditions. Darkness makes hazards harder to see, so slower speeds give you more time to react.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles very closely.
Watch only five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to avoid an unexpected hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to avoid an unexpected hazard.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible, use your signals and brake light, keep space around your bike, and scan ahead, behind, and beside you. Stay ready to react to any hazard.

questions.question: Before riding, which of these does NOT need to be checked?

options.text: Tire pressure.
Tire tread depth.
How reflective your tires are.
The condition of the tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire pressure, tread wear, and the condition of the sidewalls and tread.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of your lane position?

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Stop others from passing you.
Get to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay hidden in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: A good lane position protects your space and shows other drivers your intentions.

questions.question: How should you usually handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to let them pass.
Speed up to put distance between you and them.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only encourage them to follow faster and increase danger.

questions.question: How should you secure a load in a sidecar?

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure it so the weight does not shift.
Place it unsecured in the seat.
Secure it near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure it so the weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not move and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power does the front brake provide?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should a face shield NOT do to be effective?

options.text: Be free of scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.
Be airtight.
Fasten securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be airtight.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, allow clear side views, fasten securely, and let air pass through. An airtight shield causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?

options.text: By the left handgrip
By the right handgrip
By the left footrest
By the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: What do many over-the-counter drugs do?

options.text: Increase the danger of riding.
Decrease the danger of riding.
Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol with them.
Have the same effect on everyone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the danger of riding.
questions.explanation: Many drugs—including over-the-counter medicines, prescription drugs, and illegal drugs—have side effects that can make it unsafe to ride.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride down the center of the lane in wet conditions. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left track often works best, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects how you steer.
The front tire powers the bike, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire shakes the bike, making mirrors hard to use.
You cannot use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it affects your steering. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab at the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab at the rear brake.
Press down on the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: After drinking, what reduces the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Exercise
Coffee
Time
Food

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver breaks down alcohol at a fixed rate. You cannot speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: Drivers on an entrance ramp may not see you. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane, as it is not your responsibility to be seen.
Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
Move to the shoulder.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a lane away from the entrance ramp, if possible.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space to enter traffic safely. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if you can do so safely. If another lane is not available, slow down to give them space.

questions.question: When making an ordinary stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Sharply squeeze the front brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop. This habit will help you brake safely in emergency situations.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.
Move to the shoulder instead of riding over the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to avoid the weaving is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may sound.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: A small animal enters your lane while you ride in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Change lanes as quickly as you can.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal when safe. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into other lanes to avoid a small animal can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: What is true about riding alongside another motorcyclist?

options.text: It lets you use more of the road.
Avoid it because it limits your escape routes.
It makes it easier to talk to the other rider.
It makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist. This limits the escape routes available to both of you if a hazard appears.

questions.question: A good lane position helps you do all of the following, except:

options.text: Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
See and be seen better.
Go faster.
Prepare for turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position affects your safety. It helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and set up for turns. It does not help you go faster.
